title: The heavens and earth were not made as a game.
subtitle: Creation has a purpose, and so does your life
then: The surah introduction explains that the Makkan chiefs saw life as {trap}merely sport and pastime{/trap}, with no accountability. Allah answers: He created the heavens and earth {idea}in truth, with justice{/idea}, so that those who do evil and those who do good each receive what they earned.
now: Another weekend of streaming and scrolling, then Monday, then the same again. It can start to feel like life is just filling time. {idea}Nothing around you was made for nothing{/idea}, and {reward}neither were your days{/reward}.
old: Life is mostly about getting through the week and enjoying what I can.
new: The whole universe was made with purpose. My days are part of that purpose.
try: Look at the sky for one minute today and ask what your day is for.

title: Had He wanted a pastime, it would not look like this.
subtitle: A reckoning, a Paradise, a Hell: not the marks of a game

row.title: if a pastime
sub: He would take it from Himself

then: Mujahid explained that if this were a pastime, {idea}Allah would not have created Paradise or Hell, death, resurrection, or the Reckoning{/idea}. Qatadah and others said the verse means {idea}We will not do that{/idea}. A game does not end with an account.
now: You treat a choice as small because nobody seems to be keeping score. The extra change the cashier gave you. The promise you made a child. {trap}It feels like it doesn't matter.{/trap} {idea}A world with a Reckoning is not a world where nothing counts.{/idea}
old: Most of what I do is too small to matter.
new: A world made with a Reckoning is a world where small choices count.
try: Keep one small promise today that you could easily have let slide.

title: Truth is hurled at falsehood, and falsehood is gone.
subtitle: Falsehood looks strong until truth strikes it
then: Allah says He flings the truth against falsehood. The tafsir explains: {idea}We explain the truth and thus defeat falsehood{/idea}, until it is {trap}fading and vanishing{/trap}. The verse then warns those who claimed Allah had offspring about what they invented.
now: A rumour about you spreads through the office. Everyone seems to believe it. You feel you have to shout louder. {idea}A calm, clear truth does more than noise.{/idea} {trap}Lies need constant feeding; truth does not.{/trap}
old: Falsehood is winning because it is louder.
new: When truth is made clear, falsehood has nothing to stand on.
try: Next time you are tempted to argue loudly, state the plain truth once, calmly.

title: Even those near Him are never too proud to worship.
subtitle: Closeness to Allah shows up as humble service
then: Everyone in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah. The tafsir says {idea}those near Him are the angels{/idea}. They {reward}do not feel proud or refuse to worship Him{/reward}, and they do not get tired or bored of it.
now: You learn a little, attend a few classes, and start feeling the basics are for beginners. {trap}Pride can hide inside progress.{/trap} {idea}The nearest creatures to Allah never outgrow worship.{/idea}
old: As I grow in knowledge, I need the simple acts less.
new: The closer anyone is to Allah, the more eagerly they serve Him.
try: Do one simple act of worship today with full attention, as if it were new.

title: They glorify Him night and day without slowing down.
subtitle: Constant praise from creatures who never tire
then: The angels {idea}persist in their worship night and day{/idea}, the tafsir says, obeying Allah to the utmost, and they are able to do so. Earlier verses described them as {reward}never weary{/reward}. The whole creation is already praising while people are heedless.
now: While you sleep, while you sit in traffic, while you wait in the clinic, {idea}praise of Allah never stops{/idea}. You cannot match that. {reward}You can join it for a moment{/reward}: a SubhanAllah under your breath at the bus stop.
old: I can never worship enough, so why try to keep it up.
new: Praise of Allah never stops. I can step into it whenever I remember.
try: Say SubhanAllah ten times while waiting somewhere today.

title: Can the gods they made from earth bring anyone back?
subtitle: Testing what we rely on by what it can do
then: Allah asks whether the idols they took from the earth {idea}can bring the dead back to life{/idea}. They cannot do any of that, the tafsir says, {trap}so how can they make them rivals to Allah{/trap} and worship them alongside Him?
now: You lean on your salary, your doctor, your contacts as if they hold your life. They are good things. {trap}None of them can give life or return it.{/trap} {idea}Test what you rely on by what it can actually do.{/idea}
old: As long as I have my job and my savings, I am safe.
new: Only the One who gives life can hold my life. Everything else is a means.
try: Name one thing you lean on too hard. Make dua that Allah bless it, not replace Him.

title: More than one god, and everything would fall apart.
subtitle: The order of the universe points to one Lord
then: Allah says if there were other gods in the heavens and earth, {trap}both would have been ruined{/trap}. The tafsir links it to another verse: each god would take away what he created and {trap}some would try to overcome others{/trap}. {idea}Glorified is Allah{/idea}, far above what they claim.
now: Two managers giving opposite orders. Two parents with different rules. You know how fast things break. {idea}The sunrise arriving on time every morning is a quiet witness to one Lord.{/idea}
old: The order of the world is just how things are.
new: The order of the world is a sign that one Lord runs it.
try: Watch one sunrise or sunset this week and say SubhanAllah at the moment it turns.

title: He is not questioned for what He does. We will be.
subtitle: The difference between the Lord and those He made
then: No one can overturn or object to Allah's rule, the tafsir says, {idea}because of His might, knowledge, wisdom, justice and subtlety{/idea}. But He is the One {trap}who will ask His creation about what they did{/trap}.
now: Something hard happens: a job lost, a test result. You spend nights demanding why. {idea}Asking Allah in dua is good.{/idea} {trap}Putting Him on trial while ignoring your own account is the reverse of how it works.{/trap}
old: Allah owes me an explanation for what happens to me.
new: His wisdom is beyond question. My own deeds are what I will answer for.
try: Turn one why me into a dua today: O Allah, help me through this.

title: Bring your proof. Every message before said the same.
subtitle: Belief in one God is backed by every earlier Book
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say: {idea}bring your proof{/idea}. This Quran is the Reminder for those with him, and the earlier Books were the Reminder for those before. The tafsir says each was sent with {idea}no god except Allah{/idea}, but {trap}most did not know the truth, so they turned away{/trap}.
now: You hold a belief because your family always has, or because everyone online repeats it. {trap}Ask yourself what your proof is.{/trap} {idea}Faith that has looked at the evidence stands firmer.{/idea}
old: I believe it because that is how I was raised.
new: Belief is stronger when I know why. Truth is not afraid of being asked for proof.
try: Choose one thing you believe and find one reason for it from the Quran.

title: Every messenger carried one message: worship Me alone.
subtitle: The same core call across every prophet
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}every messenger before him was told: there is no god but Me, so worship Me{/idea}. The tafsir adds that {reward}the natural inclination of man, the fitrah, also bears witness to that{/reward}.
now: Your days are pulled in many directions: career, approval, the house, the image. {trap}Each one quietly asks for worship.{/trap} {idea}Every prophet came with the same simple centre{/idea} to bring your life back to one.
old: Faith has so many parts that I lose track of the core.
new: Underneath it all is one message every prophet brought: worship Allah alone.
try: Say La ilaha illa Allah slowly three times today, meaning it.

title: Not children of God, but honored servants.
subtitle: The angels' true status, answering a false claim
then: Some of the Arabs believed {trap}the angels were the daughters of Allah{/trap}. The verse answers: {idea}Glory to Him{/idea}. They are {reward}servants He has honored{/reward}, holding high positions, obeying Him in all their words and deeds.
now: You meet people proud of who they know or which family they come from. You are tempted to feel the same. {idea}The angels' honor comes from serving.{/idea} {reward}Yours can too.{/reward}
old: Status comes from connections and family.
new: The highest honor is being a servant of Allah. Even angels hold that title.
try: Do one act of service for someone today without telling anyone.

title: They never speak before He does; they act on His word.
subtitle: The manners of the angels with their Lord
then: The angels {idea}do not initiate any matter before Allah or go against His commands{/idea}, the tafsir says. On the contrary, {reward}they hasten to do as He commands{/reward}. The verse shows those the idolaters worshipped as obedient servants, not partners.
now: You decide where to work, whom to marry, how to spend the bonus, and then ask if it is halal. {trap}The verdict comes after the decision.{/trap} {idea}The angels wait for His word first.{/idea}
old: I make my decisions, then check if they are acceptable.
new: Look to what Allah says before deciding, not after.
try: Before one decision today, pause and ask what would please Allah here.

title: Even angels intercede only for those He is pleased with.
subtitle: No one can talk you past Allah
then: Allah knows everything before them and behind them. {idea}They cannot intercede except for him with whom He is pleased{/idea}, and they stand {trap}in awe for fear of Him{/trap}. The idolaters hoped their angel-gods would plead for them regardless.
now: You think a pious parent's duas, or a good name in the community, will carry you whatever you do. {trap}Good things, but not a free pass.{/trap} {idea}What matters is being someone Allah is pleased with.{/idea}
old: Someone good will speak up for me in the end.
new: Intercession is for those Allah is pleased with. My work is to seek His pleasure.
try: Ask yourself which one thing you do pleases Allah most. Do it once more today.

title: Any servant claiming godhood would meet Hell.
subtitle: No creature has a share in Allah's place
then: The tafsir calls this {idea}a conditional sentence{/idea}; the condition does not have to take place. The angels do not claim it. The point is that {trap}whoever claims to be a god alongside Allah is a wrongdoer{/trap}, however high their station.
now: You do not claim to be a god. But you may act as the final word at home, or make your own wishes the rule nobody can question. {trap}Small versions of the same claim.{/trap} {idea}No one sits in Allah's place.{/idea}
old: Claims of divinity have nothing to do with me.
new: Whenever I make my will the final word, I should remember who truly has it.
try: Let someone at home decide one thing today that you normally control.
